paper_metadata.title: Lactate Dehydrogenase and Hemorrhagic Stroke During Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for COVID‑19

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large multicenter registry with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and well-defined baseline characteristics. While it is a retrospective analysis of a voluntary registry, the sample size is substantial and the population is representative of the target clinical group.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Adult patients with COVID-19 requiring ECMO between March 2020 and February 2022 were included.
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the target population as adults with COVID-19 requiring ECMO support during a specific timeframe.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Data source was a voluntary registry populated by 17 participating centers located in diferent regions in the United States.
items.reasoning: The use of a 17-center multicenter registry provides a broad sampling frame that reduces single-center bias.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between March 2020 and February 2022
items.reasoning: The recruitment window is explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: 17 participating centers located in diferent regions in the United States.
items.reasoning: The setting (tertiary centers capable of ECMO) and geographic scope (USA) are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: All adult patients undergoing ECMO support for respiratory and/or cardiac support with COVID-19 infection... Patients with no available data on LDH were excluded.
items.reasoning: Criteria are clear, including the requirement for the prognostic factor (LDH) data.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: There were 520 patients that underwent ECMO placement... and 384 had an available LDH.
items.reasoning: Approximately 74% of the eligible registry patients were included. While high, 26% were excluded due to missing LDH data, which could introduce slight selection bias.

items.reasoning: Table 1 provides exhaustive detail on demographics, comorbidities, and pre-ECMO physiological parameters.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for all patients through a 100-day follow-up period using Kaplan-Meier methods. Attrition is handled via censoring for death or weaning, which is standard for this acute, high-mortality setting.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients were censored at 100 days after ECMO initiation. Censoring was done for ischemic stroke, weaning of ECMO, device upgrade, or death.
items.reasoning: The study uses time-to-event analysis, ensuring all 384 patients contribute data until an event or censoring occurs.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While LDH is an objective lab value, the study uses a data-dependent cut-point (>750 U/L) derived from ROC analysis within the same cohort, which can lead to overestimation of the prognostic effect.
